excerpt: Stripe, PayPal, Gumroad, and Lemon Squeezy block creators in dozens of countries. Here is the sovereign infrastructure that works everywhere they do not.

content.text: If you’re in Nigeria, Pakistan, or Zimbabwe, Stripe’s country restrictions lock you out of selling digital products. Gumroad, Lemon Squeezy, and Paddle follow suit, citing regulatory hurdles or ‘risk.’ PayPal limits accounts in Ghana and Kenya to receiving only. Conventional platforms treat your geography as a liability. This post compares the architecture of workarounds versus sovereign commerce stacks—built on GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Workers, and crypto payments—to show which actually delivers ownership, automation, and global reach.
What Each Option Actually Offers

Conventional platforms like Gumroad and Paddle rent you a storefront with payment processing bundled in. You pay monthly fees, accept their terms, and operate at their mercy. Workarounds—using VPNs to access Stripe or PayPal—violate terms of service and risk sudden shutdowns. Sovereign commerce stacks invert this. You own the hosting (GitHub Pages or Cloudflare), the backend logic (Google Apps Script or Workers), and the payment verification (NOWPayments). No platform controls your operations. No subscriptions. No geographic gatekeepers. The tradeoff: you manage deployment, but gain infrastructure you cannot be locked out of.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

Platforms exclude entire countries based on compliance costs or perceived fraud risk. Nigeria, Venezuela, and Bangladesh top the blacklist. Workarounds fail when IP blocks or identity verification expose your location. Sovereign stacks bypass this by decoupling hosting, payments, and delivery. GitHub Pages serves your store globally. NOWPayments processes 300+ cryptocurrencies without KYC. Cloudflare R2 delivers files instantly. The architecture ignores borders because it runs on permissionless networks. Your customers pay in USDC on Solana for $0.00001 fees. The platform’s country list becomes irrelevant.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

Stripe charges 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction—if you’re allowed to use it. PayPal holds funds for 21 days in restricted regions. Crypto payments via NOWPayments cost 0.5% with no holds. Stablecoins on BSC or TRON cost under $0.10 per transaction. Sovereign stacks automate verification via webhooks, firing delivery the moment payment confirms on-chain. The tradeoff: you educate buyers on crypto wallets. But the fee structure and speed are superior where conventional rails fail or exploit you. Your customer in Ethiopia pays in USDT; your product delivers in 30 seconds.
Platforms exclude you based on geography. Sovereign stacks exclude no one.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

Platforms own your customer data, product files, and payment history. They can suspend your account or change terms overnight. Sovereign stacks store orders in Supabase or Google Sheets—databases you control. Product files live in Cloudflare R2 or Google Drive—storage you own. Automation runs on your backend logic. After deployment, COREMERCH has no access. No platform can delete your store or withhold your revenue. The tradeoff: you handle initial setup. But the result is infrastructure that cannot be taken from you. Your business runs on assets you own, not rent.
